articles.title: Natalie Harp’s ‘hold’ over Trump puts major White House ‘promotion’ in play: journalist
articles.description: Natalie Harp, President Donald Trump’s 35-year-old female aide, could very well score a senior administration role due to her unusual “hold” over the president, veteran political journalist Chris Whipple argued on Saturday. Following the abrupt departure last month of White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt, speculation has grown as to who might fill the now-vacant role. While some have speculated that ousted Fox News host Maria Bartiromo may be tapped for the position, others, like MS NOW’s Alex Witt, wondered if Harp may end up being selected given her unusually close relationship with Trump. “Do you see a world where Harp emerges with a larger role, maybe the next White House Press Secretary?” Witt asked Whipple on Saturday. While stressing that it was “impossible” to know with certainty, Whipple said that not only was it "conceivable" that Harp could be awarded such a “promotion,” but that she essentially already acted as a “virtual staff secretary.” “In a normal White House, a staff secretary tees up reliable information on every side of an issue for the president to make decisions — Natalie has usurped that role, in effect giving Trump sunny news and everything he wants to hear,” Whipple said. “So could she be a press secretary? Sure, it's possible.” What might Harp being selected for the role of White House spokesperson even more likely, Whipple argued, was her strong influence over the president. “What's clear is that she has a kind of magic with Trump, she has a hold over him that I think is comparable to [White House Chief of Staff] Susie Wiles' influence over Trump,” Whipple continued. “Trump trusts her just as he trusts Susie Wiles because she speaks his language and she's on his side unequivocally. That's the litmus test for people who have influence around Donald Trump.” Whipple was the author of the bombshell profile on top officials of the second Trump administration, notably Wiles, who made a series of stunning remarks that appeared to disparage Vice President JD Vance and others.

articles.title: When Dad asked me to edit his novel, I wanted to say no – but ran directly towards the lion’s den | Anna Spargo-Ryan
articles.description: My father doesn’t ask for help from just anyone. And yet he asked for mine. He believed in me My dad and I believe in many of the same things: cheesecake; the Geelong football club; my mum. And that we should immediately be experts at anything. First try. No practice. No revision. He taught me this in kindergarten. Every day he pushed me to be brilliant. We played spelling games in the car and did maths workbooks for fun. Before I started school I had “published” a library of my own books, complete with copyright information. I had become – and I’m assuming this is true of most Guardian writers – a precocious kid who irritated everyone around her by being boisterously, aggressively right about everything all of the time. Just like my dad. (Obviously I’ve grown a lot since then.) Continue reading...

articles.title: Asif says devolution of power is 'inevitable', accuses PPP of having contradictory stance on new provinces
articles.description: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has said that the devolution of power is “inevitable”, while also accusing the PPP of having a contradictory stance on the issue of new provinces. “When there is talk of a Saraiki province in Punjab, the PPP supports it or shows a soft corner on this issue. And when there is talk of multiple provinces or administrative units instead of four, talk of ‘Sindhudesh’ begins,” he said in a post on the social media platform X late Saturday night. On Friday, the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) was denied the opportunity to present a resolution against the “Sindhudesh movement”. The PPP had slammed the party for attempting to “mislead the people” by tabling the resolution. Asif said that he saw “something else” behind this “dual policy” by the PPP, adding that he would delve into this deeper “when the time comes”. “We are first and foremost Pakistanis. Devolution was decided as a constitutional principle through the 18th Amendment, which was not respected. Time and circumstance demand that it be implemented with integrity,” he said. He said that concentration of power had made the current system obsolete, which needed to be “corrected”. “Provinces or administrative units, whatever label you want to apply. You have 36 divisions, use them, or devise some other administrative-geographical scheme. The devolution of power is inevitable,” he said. Asif’s remarks come as the PPP, a key ally of the PML-N-led ruling coalition, has questioned Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s silence over the debate on creating new provinces and sought his stance on the matter. The PPP had earlier maintained that any move to create additional federating units must follow the procedure laid down in the Constitution. However, the PPP-led Sindh government on Wednesday got a resolution passed by the provincial assembly opposing any further division of the country’s existing four provinces. A debate over the creation of new federating units has continued for the past couple of months in different circles, although there has been no official confirmation about the origin or contours of any proposal. However, some ruling-party leaders and federal cabinet members have publicly expressed support for the idea at different forums, including parliament. Media reports have suggested proposals ranging from eight to as many as 30 provinces, though no official plan has been announced. Talking to Dawn on Friday, PPP Parliamentarians Secretary General Nayyar Hussain Bokhari sought the prime minister’s position on the issue. Bokhari said that if the government was serious about increasing the number of provinces, it should first bring the matter before the federal cabinet, after which the prime minister should take all stakeholders and political parties on board. He recalled that consultations between the government and political parties had continued for months during the framing of the 1973 Constitution, while deliberations preceding the 18th Constitutional Amendment had lasted for more than a year. Bokhari, who also raised the issue during a talk show on DawnNewsTV on Friday, said the consent of the provinces was essential for carving out new federating units. He said any such move would also require the necessary constitutional amendment to be passed by both the National Assembly and Senate with a two-thirds majority. The PML-N-led government enjoys a two-thirds majority in the National Assembly with the PPP’s support. Therefore, if the PPP pulled back its support, it would become impossible for the government to implement the idea. Responding to a question about the local government system in the country, Bokhari said any move in that regard must also follow the Constitution, particularly Article 140-A, which provides for the establishment of local governments by the provinces. Meanwhile, PML-N leader and Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah on Friday reiterated that no preparations were currently under way for the creation of new provinces. Sanaullah told a private television channel that no bill or resolution regarding the creation of new provinces had been presented in parliament. He said consultation and consensus among political parties would be essential before any such bill or resolution could be brought before parliament. Responding to a question, he said there was currently no discussion under way regarding the division of the existing provinces.

articles.title: Judge puts a tripwire on Trump's arch as he races to build before anyone can stop him
articles.description: A federal judge has ordered the Trump administration to provide 48 hours' notice before it begins working on President Donald Trump's arch . According to a post by Politico legal reporter Kyle Cheney, Judge Tanya Chutkan ordered advance notice to her court before any work begins on the arch. She handed down the order as she prepared to consider a motion for a temporary restraining order to stop construction on the arch. The order for advance notice also comes after the Supreme Court allowed Trump's East Wing ballroom to finish and amid challenges to his D.C. golf course. Politico legal reporter Josh Gerstein noted in a Friday report that Trump is employing a legal "tush push" to get his projects most of the way through construction before they can be challenged in court, with the thought being that courts can't stop the Trump administration from building what's already been built. "Courts, I think, are now recognizing this as a very explicitly purposeful strategy," an anonymous lawyer who has faced the administration told Gerstein. "The question is: are they prepared to do something about it?" Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said on Thursday that the Trump administration plans to start excavation over the next two weeks to move ahead with the arch, according to reports . However, three Vietnam War veterans asked Chutkan on Friday to prevent work from starting on the arch, the Washington Post reported . The veterans sought a temporary restraining order through an emergency filing and warned that the administration is seeking to outrace federal courts on the project, The Post noted. Chutkan's order demanded that the Trump administration "shall provide the court with 48 hours' notice before engaging in any activity on Memorial Circle other than on-site information gathering." The information gathering was limited to looking for anything "regarding any archaeological resources that may be present at the site."

articles.title: Baffled WSJ flings Trump's own words back in his face after major heel turn
articles.description: President Donald Trump is trying once again to impose massive new taxes on businesses that hire foreign workers by executive decree — and it cuts directly against what he ran on, the Wall Street Journal editorial board wrote on Friday. The administration previously proposed a $100,000 fee on businesses for hiring workers under H-1B visas, which are used for high-skilled immigrants like tech workers. A judge struck this down as an unconstitutional tax without Congressional approval, but the administration is now trying to re-impose the fee using a different law. Trump's supporters have claimed this would free up more jobs for American workers — but in reality, this would be a disaster, wrote the board. "Businesses invest heavily in training U.S. workers, but colleges are educating too few graduates with particular skill sets that employers need — e.g., cyber-security and robotics," said the board. In fact, data from the National Foundation for American Policy indicates that "foreigners account for roughly 75% to 80% of full-time graduate students in AI-related fields." Moreover, the board continued, this is a complete reversal from what Trump said on the 2024 campaign trail — which was one of the only concessions he made in favor of immigration. "Mr. Trump during the 2024 campaign backed expanding the foreign talent pipeline," noted the board — at the time, Trump said foreign students at American universities “should get automatically as part of your diploma a green card,” because “you need brilliant people.” Flash forward to today, the board said, and his DHS plan "amounts to a tax on businesses that often bring in brilliant people." The bottom line, the board concluded, is that "smaller businesses and startups might struggle to afford the tax and would have a harder time competing for foreign talent against Big Tech companies. Many of America’s great companies, including Nvidia, Google, OpenAI and SpaceX, were founded in part by immigrants. Why does the Administration want to keep out the next Elon Musk?"
